info.description: Epstein and Axtell's Sugarscape rule G1 on one sugar hill: 120 Ant agents on a 30x30 bounded grid; the `sugar` patch starts at each cell's capacity (10 at the centre, falling by 1 per step of Manhattan distance) and GROWS BACK 1 per tick up to that capacity (`grow: {rate: 1}`, max defaulting to the initial landscape). Each tick an ant steps to the best of its 4 von Neumann neighbours and its own cell (a 5-way PATCH comparison: vision 1), harvests the whole cell and pays Metabolism; it starves at zero wealth. The population falls from 120 to about 24 by t=40 as the ants that cannot see the hill starve, then HOLDS for good: the hill's 181 cells regrow 1 sugar each per tick, more than its survivors burn, so regrowth balances consumption (the oracle checks t=40 and t=120; the same ants with no regrowth all starve by about t=110). Metabolism and the wealth range are this instance's own; the grid and the hill are fixed.
